newsitem.title: UK: Thomas the Tank Engine steams onto UK market.
newsitem.headline: Thomas the Tank Engine steams onto UK market.

text.p: International children's star Thomas the Tank Engine roared onto the London Stock Exchange on Wednesday as investors sent its production company's shares chugging full steam ahead.

Shares of Britt Allcroft Plc, which produces "Thomas the Tank Engine and Friends", raced to 159.5 pence per share on their first day of trade, setting a debut premium of about 23 percent over their placing price of 130 pence.
The offering price would have given the company a market capitalisation of 30.6 million pounds ($50.40 million).
About 4.7 million shares were sold by existing shareholders in the flotation, and 3.8 million new ordinary shares were issued by Britt Allcroft.
The company previously said it expected to raise about 4.2 million pounds net from the flotation.

When it announced the offering in September, the company, engineered by the husband and wife team of Britt Allcroft and Angus Wright, said it wanted to develop additional characters and extend its existing brands.

Britt Allcroft holds the television, video and character licensing rights to Thomas the Tank Engine, which has won admirers from the United States to Japan and attracted backing from venture capital firms and former Beatle Ringo Starr.
Starr's voice featured in the TV series of Thomas the Tank Engine. The musician also bought a minor stake in the company.
The company's new series of animated films, Britt Allcroft's Magic Adventures of Mumfie, had also been broadcast in Britain, Australia, Japan and the U.S.
Britt Allcroft posted a pretax profit of two million pounds and turnover of 11.5 million pounds in its financial year ended on June 30.
Price Waterhouse Corporate Finance sponsored the placing, which was underwritten by Charterhouse Tilney Securities Ltd. ($1=.6072 Pound)
